observations.claim: Roughly 48 user-facing strings are hardcoded English literals despite the app shipping values-hi/strings.xml — the whole partner sign-in flow is untranslatable for the Ayodhya/rural-UP target user.
Attempts-remaining is pluralised by English string concatenation in code, not pluralStringResource — the customer app does this correctly, proving the pattern was available and skipped here.

The screen is hard-pinned to light theme: root and hero use HomeservicesColors.Brand.* which Color.kt:67-68 explicitly documents as LIGHT-only, and the form card is literal Color.White, while its text still reads from colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant — in dark mode that is #B7C6BD on white.

Two Devanagari brand strings are hardcoded in Kotlin, so an English-locale technician sees mixed-script chrome and a Hindi-locale technician still sees English body copy — the hero is permanently in the wrong language for someone.

Direct divergence from customer-app: the customer AuthScreen resolves every string through stringResource and every colour through MaterialTheme/LocalHomeservicesExtendedColors; the technician file is a stale fork of the same layout with literals substituted back in. Same layout, different engineering standard — they will drift visibly as soon as either is touched.
Five of ten states collapse to one identical full-screen bare spinner with no skeleton and no progress context — the user loses the form entirely on every async hop.
Four typography usages land on unmapped M3 slots and therefore render in Roboto next to Geist Sans in the same visual block (headlineSmall title sits directly above bodyLarge body).

OTP entry is a single generic OutlinedTextField with no per-digit boxes, no resend countdown, no auto-fill/SMS-retriever hint and no auto-advance — below the 2026 bar for every Indian consumer app and materially harder for a low-literacy user.

Card-on-card: HsSectionCard (elev1, colorScheme.surface #FFFDF8) is nested inside a Color.White card, producing a near-invisible 1dp elevation seam rather than deliberate layering — the 'flat-gray-card' failure mode.

The error state is a full-screen takeover carrying the raw ViewModel message as body copy, with only a 'Try again' button — no inline field validation, no way to switch sign-in method, no support route.
No motion whatsoever: no Crossfade/AnimatedContent between the ten auth states and no import of HomeservicesMotion/HomeservicesEasing, so every transition is a hard cut.
Off-grid spacing throughout (28/36/22/56/2/1 dp) alongside correctly-tokenised gaps, so the rhythm reads as accidental rather than systematic.

Technician uses rememberSaveable for phone/OTP input where customer uses plain remember — a behavioural divergence (technician survives rotation, customer does not) inside supposedly identical screens.
String resource keys were forked rather than shared: technician uses auth_back_to_sign_in / auth_use_another_method where customer uses auth_back_to_options / auth_use_other_method for the same UI.

The step model contradicts the rest of the cluster: this screen advertises '3 steps' (Verify identity / Go online / Track earnings) while KycScreen labels itself 'Step 1 of 2' and 'Step 2 of 2' and ServiceSelection labels itself 'Step 3 of 3' — three mutually inconsistent progress vocabularies in one onboarding.

observations.claim: Inconsistent card surface within one design language: this frame's card is colorScheme.background while the visually identical Auth and Kyc frames use literal Color.White, so the three hero screens do not match.

The hero block (gradient, two circles at identical radii/offsets, 28/28/36 padding, 4dp gap, headlineLarge/bodyLarge/labelSmall stack) is copy-pasted across three files rather than extracted — the customer app extracted it as AuthHeroZone.
Non-scrollable fixed-height card plus bottom-pinned CTA is a Hindi clipping hazard: Devanagari runs 15-30% longer/taller and there is no verticalScroll escape.
Four of the screen's text styles resolve to unmapped M3 slots (titleMedium for the card title, titleSmall for each step title), so the checklist renders in Roboto against Geist Sans elsewhere.
The offline/queued KYC warning — the only dynamic information on the screen — is styled as the lowest-emphasis element (labelSmall, onSurfaceVariant, no icon, no container).
Light-only brand colours and Color.White literals mean this screen would not render correctly in dark theme either.

surfaces.density: Airy but hollow, and the hero/card fractions are inconsistent with its siblings (0.32/0.70 here vs 0.38/0.65 in Auth and Onboarding — KycScreen.kt:54-55 vs AuthScreen.kt:71-72). Each step card holds only two explainer rows plus buttons inside a 70%-height card, so there is significant dead space beneath the CTA on a normal phone.

observations.claim: The single most compliance-critical screen in the technician app contains zero localized strings — stringResource is not imported at all — so a Hindi-locale rural technician performs Aadhaar and PAN submission entirely in English.

The success/review state displays the raw Kotlin enum constant as its headline status ('PAN_DONE', 'MANUAL_REVIEW', or the literal 'UNKNOWN') in titleLarge Bold — a machine token presented as the primary information.

KYC failure is not humane: a fixed English headline plus the unfiltered ViewModel/server message as body, with 'Try again' as the only action — no support contact, no explanation of consequences, no alternate path.
After choosing a PAN photo the user never sees the image — only a bodySmall sentence — so there is no way to confirm the correct, legible document was selected before submitting a tax document.

Action hierarchy is inverted on the PAN step: the terminal, irreversible action ('Submit for review') is a secondary outlined button while the reversible picker action ('Change photo') is the primary filled button.

The route is declared but appears unreachable — no navigate("kyc") exists in main source, the graph starts at service_selection, and the deep-link handler only posts to a bus without navigating. KYC may be unreachable in the shipped flow.
observations.evidence: OnboardingGraph.kt:18-19; MainActivity.kt:53-63; grep for 'navigate("kyc")' over technician-app/app/src/main/kotlin returns no hits

observations.claim: Progress is text-only: 'Step 1 of 2'/'Step 2 of 2' in a low-contrast translucent chip, with no stepper, no bar, no numerals-as-graphics — for a low-literacy user there is no non-textual sense of how far along they are, and the numbering contradicts ServiceSelection's 'Step 3 of 3'.
Icon-to-text ratio on the whole KYC flow is zero — KycScreen renders no Icon composable at any point; every instruction (Aadhaar consent, photo quality, glare, corners) is prose.
observations.evidence: KycScreen.kt:1-414 (no androidx.compose.material3.Icon import; only HsTimelineStep's 12dp squares from HsComponents.kt:187-194)

observations.claim: Uploading a document shows an indeterminate spinner with no percentage, no thumbnail, no size/time estimate and no cancel — on a rural 2G/3G connection this is an unbounded blank wait.

Seven typography usages land on unmapped M3 slots (headlineSmall x2, titleSmall x4 via HsTimelineStep, labelMedium), so the step titles and every explainer heading render in Roboto beside Geist Sans body copy.

Hero/card proportions diverge from the sibling hero screens (0.32/0.70 vs 0.38/0.65) and the hero bottom padding differs (28 vs 36), so moving between Auth and KYC produces a visible jump in the same visual language.
Light-theme-only colours: brand literals plus a Color.White card while text still reads from the theme, so dark mode produces light-grey body text on a white card.

'Skip for now, complete later' is offered on the Aadhaar step with no statement of what the technician loses by skipping, and no equivalent skip on the PAN step — an asymmetric, unexplained escape hatch.
The queued-upload banner overlays the hero at the top of the screen with no animation and no liveRegion, so it can appear/disappear silently mid-interaction.

Two different components named PhotoUploadRetryBanner exist with different palettes (brand-hover/white here, tertiaryContainer in activeJob), documented as intentional but read as inconsistency to a user who encounters both.

surfaces.purpose: Technician picks which of 13 services they perform and captures their starting service area (GPS), completing onboarding.
surfaces.entryPoints: OnboardingGraph.kt:18 declares navigation(startDestination = "service_selection", route = "main"); reached from AppNavigation.kt:160-165 (onNeedsOnboarding -> navigate("main")). Also re-used in Edit mode via ServiceSelectionMode.Edit (ServiceSelectionScreen.kt:175-178).

Conditional LoadingCard item — an HsSectionCard with a default-size CircularProgressIndicator + 'Loading saved service profile' — rendered ABOVE the service list, not instead of it
ServiceListCard: HsSectionCard titled 'Services you provide' containing the 13 catalogue items grouped by category; each group prints a titleSmall Bold primary-coloured header then its ServiceRows
ServiceRow: clickable full-width Row, 6dp vertical padding — M3 Checkbox + 8dp spacer + single-line ellipsised bodyLarge SemiBold name. No icon, no image, no price, no description.

ServiceAreaPreview dispatch: no coords -> EmptyLocationPreview (132dp surfaceVariant box, MyLocation icon, 'Tap Use current location' titleSmall + bodySmall hint, or a spinner+label while locating); coords + no MAPS_API_KEY -> CapturedLocationPreview (132dp primaryContainer box with label and raw lat/lng to 5 decimals); coords + key -> live GoogleMap at 180dp with a marker

Conditional ErrorCard item: HsSectionCard with an Icons.Default.Work glyph tinted error, the message in bodyMedium onSurfaceVariant, an optional 'Retry profile load' HsSecondaryButton, and a trailing non-clickable Refresh icon
SaveButton item: full-width HsPrimaryButton whose label swaps to 'Saving services' while saving; disabled during save/load/locate

loading.quality: A spinner card is INSERTED ABOVE the fully-rendered service list rather than replacing it, so the user sees a live-looking checkbox list and a 'loading' card simultaneously and can toggle skills that are about to be overwritten by the fetch (ServiceSelectionViewModel.kt:43-45).

empty.quality: No empty state. The catalogue is a hardcoded 13-item list (ServiceCatalogue.kt:10-25) so it can never be empty — but that also means a technician whose trade is not in the list has no path forward and no 'other' option.

error.quality: Present but poor: the message text is rendered in onSurfaceVariant (not error colour), the leading glyph is a briefcase (Icons.Default.Work), and a decorative Refresh icon sits beside a real retry button. Whether retry shows at all is decided by string-matching the English prose 'Could not load' (line 164).

success.quality: No confirmation. On save the screen simply navigates away via LaunchedEffect (ServiceSelectionScreen.kt:75-77) with no toast, checkmark, or transition.

offline.quality: No offline concept. A failed load produces the generic 'Could not load your saved services. You can still save this form.' (ServiceSelectionViewModel.kt:64) and a failed save produces 'Could not save services. Check your connection and try again.' (ServiceSelectionViewModel.kt:169) — text only, no queueing, no retry banner like KYC has.

permissionDenied.quality: Minimal: a denial collapses into the same generic ErrorCard with the string 'Allow location access to set your service area.' — no rationale before the prompt, no deep link to app settings, no handling of permanent 'don't ask again' denial.

surfaces.skeletonOrSpinner: Two bare default-size CircularProgressIndicators — one inside LoadingCard (ServiceSelectionScreen.kt:432) and one inside EmptyLocationPreview while locating (ServiceSelectionScreen.kt:359). HsSkeletonBlock is never used.

hardcodedDp.context: EmptyLocationPreview height — off-scale and 48dp shorter than the map it replaces

i18n.hindiRisk: Only ONE string on the screen is localized — stringResource(R.string.service_finding_area) at line 361 (translated at values-hi/strings.xml:122). Everything else, including all 13 service names and 6 group names in ServiceCatalogue.kt:12-24 and every validation message in the ViewModel, is a hardcoded English literal. This is the screen where a rural technician must identify their own trade, and the trade names are English-only. Layout: ServiceRow names are maxLines=1 with TextOverflow.Ellipsis (lines 279-280), so a Hindi service name ~25% longer than 'Tap / Faucet Installation' or 'Ceiling Fan Installation' will truncate — the technician would be selecting a trade they cannot fully read. HsPrimaryButton wraps a plain Text (HsComponents.kt:46) inside a fixed 64dp height, so a longer Hindi 'Save and continue' can wrap and clip.
i18n.currencyFormatting: No currency on this surface, even though the services carry fixed prices elsewhere in the product; the technician chooses trades with no visible earning information.

a11y.contentDescriptions: All four icons pass contentDescription = null: LocationOn (line 296), MyLocation (line 365), MyLocation (line 403), Work-as-error (line 453), Refresh (line 475). The Refresh icon at 473-477 is purely decorative yet visually identical to an action, and the error icon is null-described so a screen-reader user gets no signal that the following text is an error.

touchTargetRisks.size: Row padding vertical 6.dp around an M3 Checkbox
touchTargetRisks.note: The Row itself adds only 12dp of height; the M3 Checkbox enforces its own minimum interactive size so the effective row is likely ≥48dp, but the visible row is far denser than that and adjacent rows have no separation — a mis-tap between two adjacent trades is easy. INFERRED for the exact resolved height.
Rendered at action size and error-adjacent but has no clickable modifier — an affordance that looks tappable and is not.

contrastRisks.note: Error message text is rendered in colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant, not colorScheme.error — the error copy has the same visual weight as ordinary helper text.
bodySmall in onSurfaceVariant (#5F6C66) on surfaceVariant (#E8F1EC) ≈ 4.6:1 — right at the AA boundary for small text.
The raw coordinate line is bodySmall onPrimaryContainer inside a primaryContainer box — small type over a tinted fill.

a11y.focusOrder: No semantics blocks anywhere. The ServiceRow exposes both a clickable Row and a Checkbox with its own onCheckedChange (lines 264, 269), producing a duplicated/ambiguous accessibility node per row instead of a single toggleable node with role=Checkbox. No group semantics for the category headers.

placeholderOrMissing: No service icons or photos for any of the 13 trades — ServiceCatalogueItem has only id/name/group (ServiceCatalogue.kt:3-7), so the entire trade picker is 13 rows of English text with checkboxes.

The customer app ships 13 drawable-nodpi/service_hero_*.png assets; technician-app ships exactly one content drawable (tech_field_ac_service.png), used only by TechnicianHomeScreen.kt:434 — none of these images reach the technician's own service picker.
Map preview degrades to a flat coloured box with raw decimal coordinates when MAPS_API_KEY is blank (lines 328-330, 386-421).

motion.transitionsOnNav: None. LoadingCard, ErrorCard and the location preview swap in and out of the LazyColumn with no AnimatedVisibility (lines 141-167), and the 132dp placeholder is replaced by a 180dp map with no crossfade — a 48dp layout jump.

surfaces.density: Inconsistent. The list uses 24dp screen padding and 16dp card gaps (lines 135-136) but the rows inside the trade card are packed at 6dp vertical (line 265) with no dividers, so 13 checkboxes read as a dense undifferentiated block while the surrounding cards are airy. Two different placeholder heights (132dp) versus the map (180dp) make the page height shift.

observations.claim: The retry affordance is gated on English string matching — `uiState.errorMessage.startsWith("Could not load")` — so the moment error copy is localized to Hindi the retry button silently disappears.

All 13 service names and 6 group names are hardcoded English strings in Kotlin with no stringResource path, on the one screen where a low-literacy Hindi-speaking technician must identify their own trade.
Zero iconography or imagery for the trades: each service is a bare checkbox plus a one-line, single-line-clipped English label, so the picker offers no pictorial route for a non-reader.

The step badge says 'Step 3 of 3' while the KYC screens in the same onboarding say 'Step 1 of 2' and 'Step 2 of 2', and the (dead) onboarding checklist says '3 steps' with a different list of steps — the user is given three contradictory progress models.

Loading is additive rather than substitutive: the spinner card is inserted above an already-interactive service list, and the fetch then overwrites the user's selections, so a technician can toggle skills that are silently discarded.

The error card uses Icons.Default.Work (a briefcase) as its error glyph and pairs a real 'Retry profile load' button with a decorative, non-clickable Refresh icon — two competing signals, one of them a lie.

The captured-location fallback shows raw decimal coordinates ('Location selected: 26.79220, 82.19980') as user-facing confirmation, formatted with Locale.US — meaningless to the target technician and locale-incorrect for Devanagari numerals.

Location permission has no pre-prompt rationale and no recovery: denial routes into the generic error card with a single English sentence, with no settings deep link and no handling of permanent denial.
Error copy is not visually treated as error — the message renders in onSurfaceVariant inside a standard HsSectionCard with no error container, border, or colour.
Five typography usages resolve to unmapped M3 slots (titleSmall x3 directly, titleMedium x2 via HsSectionCard titles), so every card title and group header on the screen renders in Roboto.
Service names are maxLines = 1 with ellipsis, so longer Hindi trade names will truncate on the screen where the technician commits to what work they will receive.
The location preview changes height between states (132dp placeholder vs 180dp map) with no animation, causing a 48dp content jump the moment GPS resolves.
The screen has no app bar, title bar, or back affordance — it is a bare LazyColumn, so the technician cannot navigate back out of onboarding.
Each ServiceRow exposes both a clickable Row and an independently checkable Checkbox, producing duplicated accessibility nodes instead of one toggleable node.
Selected-state feedback is only the checkbox tick — the row itself does not change background, border, or elevation, so a scan of 13 dense rows gives no at-a-glance sense of what is selected.

This screen breaks the visual language of the rest of the onboarding cluster: Auth, Onboarding and KYC are all gradient-hero + white sheet frames; this one is a plain cream LazyColumn of cards with no hero at all.
